$comment: Turn 1 candidate set. Every `feel` line is written by hand. Aim for 15-20 games you know well rather than 40 you half-know. A `feel` line should say what playing it is actually like, not what genre it is: if the sentence would still be true of ten other games, it is not specific enough.

candidates.title: Outer Wilds
candidates.feel: A clockwork solar system where knowledge is your only upgrade, driven by the bittersweet inevitability of an ending you cannot fight.

candidates.title: Vampire Survivors
candidates.feel: A slot machine disguised as an action game where your only input is movement, culminating in a hypnotic screen-clearing light show of passive destruction.

candidates.title: Death Stranding
candidates.feel: A quiet, punishing hike across a ruined landscape where the terrain itself is the main antagonist, making the eventual appearance of a smooth road feel like a miracle.

candidates.title: Stardew Valley
candidates.feel: A self-directed second life of agricultural routine and gentle community building, where the only pressure is the sun going down.

candidates.title: Doom Eternal
candidates.feel: A breakneck resource puzzle where you must aggressively dismantle enemies in specific ways to stay alive, treating demons as health and ammo piñatas.

candidates.title: Return of the Obra Dinn
candidates.feel: An uncompromising logic grid of tragedy where you piece together a frozen diorama of betrayals, relying entirely on your own deduction with zero hand-holding.

candidates.title: Civilization VI
candidates.feel: A methodical, multi-hour balancing act of city planning and historical arms races, where 'one more turn' becomes a hypnotic loop of long-term investments paying off.

candidates.title: Hades
candidates.feel: A blistering cycle of failure and rebirth where dying feels like progress because every return to the hub rewards you with unraveling family drama and permanent strength.

candidates.title: Celeste
candidates.feel: A grueling but encouraging mountain climb of precise platforming, where hundreds of rapid-fire deaths are meant to teach you the exact rhythm of a room.

candidates.title: Disco Elysium
candidates.feel: A chaotic argument inside your own head where failing a dice roll often leads to a more interesting story than succeeding, wrapped in a melancholic murder mystery.

candidates.title: Bloodborne
candidates.feel: A terrifying descent into gothic madness that forces you to abandon defensive habits, rewarding hyper-aggression and calculated risks to regain lost health.

candidates.title: Factorio
candidates.feel: An ever-expanding logistical headache where fixing one bottleneck inevitably creates two more, transforming a barren alien world into a symphony of automated conveyor belts.

candidates.title: Slay the Spire
candidates.feel: A tightrope walk of short-term survival against long-term mathematical efficiency, where every card added feels like both a lifeline and a potential future liability.

candidates.title: Subnautica
candidates.feel: A beautiful, terrifying plunge into an alien ocean that masterfully shifts from serene resource gathering in the shallows to crushing, claustrophobic dread in the deep.

candidates.title: Red Dead Redemption 2
candidates.feel: A deliberately paced, methodical immersion into a dying era, where the weight of your animations and the mundane chores ground a sprawling, tragic outlaw epic.

candidates.title: Tetris Effect
candidates.feel: A familiar spatial organization task elevated into a synesthetic trance, where clearing lines pulses in time with a soaring electronic soundtrack.

candidates.title: Planet Coaster
candidates.feel: A joyous, blank-canvas construction kit where managing the nausea and queuing times of thousands of guests is secondary to designing the perfect, needlessly elaborate roller coaster.

candidates.title: Hollow Knight
candidates.feel: A lonely, melancholic descent through a ruined bug kingdom, requiring you to physically map a labyrinth in your head while mastering precise, unforgiving combat.

candidates.title: Portal 2
candidates.feel: A comedic physics playground that teaches you to think in spatial paradoxes, rewarding 'aha' moments of momentum manipulation with biting corporate satire.

candidates.title: Journey
candidates.feel: A silent, sand-swept pilgrimage that strips away complex mechanics to foster an unspoken, emotional bond with a completely anonymous stranger sharing your path.
